clue.text: See 3
Threaten little devil with death

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
death is one's end

explanation.surface: Someone menaces a small demon with a fatal outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or hang over as a menace, so it means threaten in the sense of being imminent.

clue.text: Just after stopping US hit men, look out for 25: 14 28 they called him!

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other like a stopper
out can mean in disarray or wrong, so the gathered letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on the hour' or 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A tough-guy gangland warning that turns out to be about a jazz musician and his nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition borrows other answers: it is the PIANIST whom people called MELODIOUS THUNK, a joking nickname for the bebop great.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelonious Monk, the bebop pianist, was jokingly nicknamed Melodious Thunk for his angular, percussive playing.

clue.text: Confining antelope Geordie mother shows bottle

indicators.note: confining means shutting something in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: mam is the north-east English (Geordie, from Newcastle) word for mother
the gnu is an African antelope, also called wildebeest

explanation.surface: A Newcastle mum keeps an antelope penned in and shows off a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne, where 'mam' is the usual word for mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large wine or champagne bottle holding twice the standard amount.

clue.text: Station attendant leaving one little room

indicators.note: when something is leaving it departs, so it drops out of the word

parts.note: a waiter attends at table
one is the Roman numeral I
loo is British slang for a toilet, the smallest room

explanation.surface: A railway porter walks off his post to visit the toilet at the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little room' is a euphemism for the lavatory; the loo is the British word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is a major London railway terminus, a named example of a station.

clue.text: Sail back with wife

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
aft means at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor heads home accompanied by his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like it is telling you to reverse something, but it simply means AFT, and the wife comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To waft is to drift gently through the air, much as something sails along on a breeze.

clue.text: Place outside behind Californian university

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to place something is to stand it
to be behind someone is to support them, to be for them

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something out the back of a college in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as a position word but here means in support of, as in 'we're all behind you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanford is the private research university at Palo Alto in California's Bay Area.

clue.text: Paper's byline initially hard to see when changed

indicators.note: once the letters are changed they are rearranged into a fresh order
initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of byline
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper's journalist credit is printed too small to read until the layout is altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format newspaper, traditionally the serious kind, so it is a type of paper.

clue.text: Go round with zero speed?

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
zero looks like O
speed is measured in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A question about travelling in circles while not moving at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning energy or drive, as in 'full of go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is vigour or energetic drive, the same thing as go in the noun sense.

clue.text: Smooth and white party in atomic plant

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the outer pair formed by the other two

parts.note: A as in A-bomb, the atomic bomb
Lab is short for the UK Labour Party
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A pale smooth celebration takes place inside a nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atomic plant' suggests a power station, but it splits into A, from A-bomb, and the flower ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine translucent stone, and as an adjective it describes skin or surfaces that are white and smooth.

clue.text: Corrupt, like Mr Putin, at last in his citadel

indicators.note: something corrupt has been debased and twisted, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last directs you to the final letter of the name before it

parts.note: the last letter of Putin

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Russian leader is crooked, holed up in his fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' sits at the front like a political accusation, but it is the signal to rearrange LIKE MR plus Putin's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified complex in Moscow that houses the Russian president, so it is Putin's own stronghold.

clue.text: In East, travelling around old nation

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the shuffled letters wrap the next piece
travelling letters move about, so they are found in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A traveller tours an ancient country in the eastern part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, an independent state and so a nation.

clue.text: Wait with North American Democrat

parts.note: to bide is to wait, as in 'bide your time'
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A call to be patient alongside a Democrat from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American' looks like one phrase, but North gives N and American belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Biden is a US politician of the Democratic Party who served as the 46th president.

clue.text: Struggled again losing million in racket

parts.note: to battle is to struggle

indicators.note: losing something means letting it go, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: more can mean again, as in 'once more'
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone fought on once more after losing a fortune in some swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a criminal scheme, matching the lost million, but it is the sports kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is the small racket used in battledore and shuttlecock, the forerunner of badminton.

clue.text: Sweet-sounding line by the writer causing hatred

parts.note: the writer is the setter speaking of themself, me
L is the abbreviation for line
something odious arouses hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: A pleasant-sounding phrase from an author that nevertheless provokes loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter referring to themself, so it means ME; 'by' just sets the line beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodious means tuneful and pleasant to hear, so it describes something sweet-sounding.

clue.text: Italian poet embracing one Latvian amateur

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the poet's name wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy
one is the Roman numeral I
a Lett is a Latvian

explanation.surface: A Florentine poet hugs a dabbler from Latvia.
explanation.walkthrough: Lett is an old name for a native of Latvia; together with I it sits inside DANTE after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or field without professional commitment, the sense of amateur as a noun.

clue.text: Were Eden folk got in trouble by this?

definitions.text: Were Eden folk got in trouble by this?

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks what landed Adam and Eve in trouble in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the jumbled letters give the very thing that got Eden's inhabitants into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve ate fruit from the tree of knowledge of good and evil and were expelled from Eden.

clue.text: Expert in possession, be carrying ball and run about

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so the outer word bears the others inside

parts.note: to be is to exist
a ball is round like the letter O
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sports pundit on keeping the ball and running around with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possession' reads as a football term, but here it means demonic possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist drives out evil spirits, so is a specialist in dealing with demonic possession.

clue.text: Relationship with regal lunatic in drama

parts.note: kin are relations by blood

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family tie to a mad monarch features in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes the play itself, whose royal hero goes mad and is undone by his daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy, a named example of a drama.

clue.text: Rely on offence being taken in studies

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed inside, so it goes into the middle of the phrase

parts.note: to look to someone is to depend on them
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: Trusting someone even though they have been offended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' hints at being deceived or fooled, but here it just means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into something is to investigate or examine it, the verb sense of studies.

clue.text: Sea hawk over small creature hunted

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
S is the abbreviation for small
prey is an animal hunted by another

explanation.surface: A sea bird of prey hovers above a little animal it is hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating raptor, commonly called the sea hawk or fish hawk.

clue.text: Sip beer regularly in teetotal land

indicators.note: in places the chosen letters inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: TT is the abbreviation for teetotal

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of sip beer

explanation.surface: Someone takes the occasional sip of beer in a country where alcohol is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, splits to hold the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a Himalayan region, now governed by China, so a land or country.

clue.text: We hear coastal road comes to port

indicators.note: we hear points to how the words sound when spoken rather than how they are spelt

parts.note: a road along a bay is a bay route

explanation.surface: Reports say a road along the coast leads to a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital of Lebanon and a major Mediterranean seaport.

clue.text: Boy keeping rodents back in tens

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the whole combination reads from right to left
keeping means holding on to, so the boy holds the rodents inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A lad keeps pet mice at the back in groups of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' applies to the whole boy-and-rodents combination, not just the rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimal describes a number system based on ten, counting in units, tens and hundreds.

clue.text: Cause serious harm month after month in France

parts.note: mai is French for May
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Someone inflicts injury month after month while in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Month after month' looks like a stock phrase for repetition; read it as the first month placed after the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to wound someone so badly that they are permanently injured or disabled.

clue.text: Musician who may require a grand opening?

definitions.text: Musician who may require a grand opening?

parts.words: Musician who may require a grand opening?
parts.note: surface reading: a performer who demands a lavish launch for a show
setter's reading: a grand is a large piano, whose lid must be opened before it is played

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand opening' suggests a ceremonial launch; the grand is the piano, and the opening is lifting its lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist is a keyboard musician who plays the piano, often a concert grand.

clue.text: Rough-mannered person in County Kerry

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A boorish character turns up in an Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyke is a dialect word for a coarse or uncouth fellow, and also a nickname for a Yorkshireman.

clue.text: Banish out-of-practice princess are we told?

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so it is the sound that counts here

parts.note: rusty is out of practice; Kate is the Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: Asks whether a princess who is out of practice should be sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine, Princess of Wales, is widely known as Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is to send to the country, especially to suspend a student from a university, so to banish.

clue.text: Dull sound from strong man on time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a hunk is a big muscular man

explanation.surface: A heavy thud made by a muscleman arriving on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'A on B' puts A after B, so the hunk follows the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunk is an imitative word for a flat, heavy thud, a muffled noise like an object landing.
